title: How a request becomes a finished page
subtitle: The portable-artifacts pipeline, from one request to one offline HTML page

nodes.label: Person's request
nodes.detail: One sentence in chat: what to draw, for whom.

nodes.label: Claude Haiku agent
nodes.detail: Reads SKILL.md, writes diagram.json, then runs validate, build and check in the same turn. Never writes coordinates, CSS, SVG or HTML.

nodes.label: validate.mjs
nodes.detail: Schema and limits first, then a full layout and a geometry lint, so a spec that validates is buildable. Every error is a JSON path, the problem and the fix.

nodes.label: Offline HTML page
nodes.detail: Inline CSS, fonts and icons behind a strict CSP. The same spec and versions give the same bytes.

beats.title: Someone asks for a diagram
beats.caption: One sentence is enough; the agent plans the spec from it.

beats.title: The agent writes one JSON file
beats.caption: A title, a type, nodes and edges. No coordinates, CSS, SVG or HTML.

beats.title: Validate reads the spec
beats.caption: Schema and limits, then a full layout and a geometry lint.

beats.title: Validate names the exact fix
beats.caption: A JSON path, the problem and the fix; the agent edits one field and runs it again.

beats.title: ELK lays everything out
beats.caption: Every position comes from the layout engine, on this machine.

beats.title: Themes supply the colours
beats.caption: paper, blueprint, ink or editorial: one spec, four looks.

beats.title: Charts and video have their own renderers
beats.caption: An explainer asks for them; a plain diagram never does.

beats.title: One offline HTML page
beats.caption: Opens in any browser with no network; the CSP blocks requests.
